children: North Macedonia’s economy expanded by 4.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, accelerating from 3.1% in the previous three-month period and marking the strongest growth since Q4 2024.
Growth was driven by household expenditure (3.3% vs 2.6% in Q1) and gross investments (16.5% vs 1.5%).
Net external demand also contributed positively, with both exports (10.4% vs 6.2%) and imports (12.5% vs 5.2%) rising.
Meanwhile, growth eased in final consumption (2.8% vs 3.2%) and public expenditure (0.8% vs 5.5%).

On the production side, the most notable increases were recorded in mining and quarrying (3.9% vs -0.8%), manufacturing (4.1% vs -0.2%), and construction (21.9% vs 7.2%), while output declined in agriculture, forestry, and fisheries (-0.1% vs 2.9%) and public administration and defense (-1.3% vs 2.5%).
On a seasonally adjusted quarterly basis, GDP growth accelerated to 1.3% in Q2 from 0.4% in the previous quarter, marking the strongest growth since Q1 2014.

title: North Macedonia Q2 GDP Growth at Over 1-Year High
